jsonld.site_description: Find every civic district that covers a point or address in South Carolina, and who represents you there.
jsonld.app_description: Click any point in South Carolina, or search an address, to see every civic district that contains it, and who represents you there — county, South Carolina Senate, South Carolina House and U.S. House districts, cities and towns, school districts and ZIP codes.

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 7 congressional districts — the largest districts South Carolina carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 7 features for South Carolina, measured 2026-10-10. South Carolina did not redraw for 2026: the 120th-Congress map and the 119th's (layer 4) carry the same seven districts, every one differing by under 0.001% of its area.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: South Carolina Senate District
layers.rank_note: 46 Senate districts — the same count as the state's counties, and drawn independently of them

source.answers: The South Carolina Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (state upper chamber), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 46 features, measured 2026-10-10. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 20 m interval and refused over a 25 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: sc-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the South Carolina General Assembly's own Senate member pages (name, party, State House office, business telephone and the member's own page). The General Assembly publishes no e-mail addresses, only a message form on each member's page, so none is carried.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 46 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 46 features, measured 2026-10-10.

source.people: None yet — identity only. Every South Carolina county is governed by an elected county council; the state Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office publishes every council district and the State Election Commission's results name the winners, and neither is wired in this first change. Recorded as gap sc-county-council.

layers.label: School District
layers.rank_note: 72 unified (K-12) districts covering the whole state, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file)

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), queried live at runtime; 72 features for South Carolina, measured 2026-10-10.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD NAMES THE DISTRICT ONLY. South Carolina's school boards are not all chosen the same way, and no statewide roster of their members has been established here — recorded as gap sc-school-board-members.
source.applies: South Carolina — statewide. The label carries no qualifier because there is nothing to distinguish it from: the elementary and secondary tilings TIGERweb serves for other states are EMPTY in South Carolina (0 features each, measured 2026-10-10), and the 72 unified districts' Census land area sums to exactly the 46-county total (77,866 km2).

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 841 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas in the state's own bounding box, fetched live by envelope; the layer hides outside South Carolina

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, queried live at runtime. ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='45'. 841 features in South Carolina's box, measured 2026-10-10.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: South Carolina. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code (the Georgia test point gives 30817).

layers.label: City or Town
layers.rank_note: 271 incorporated cities and towns, live from TIGERweb

source.answers: The city or town containing the point, if any.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), queried live at runtime; 271 features for South Carolina (69 cities, 202 towns), measured 2026-10-10.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. South Carolina's cities and towns elect councils, and no statewide roster was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap sc-municipal-officeholders.
source.applies: South Carolina — statewide. A point outside every city and town is unincorporated, which the card states.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-10-10: 432 points in South Carolina's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap today, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: South Carolina — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in Georgia or North Carolina, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: the State House, Columbia, Richland County

negative_point.note: Wilkes County, GEORGIA, about 25 km west of the Savannah River — outside South Carolina and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-10-10: TIGERweb's state layer names Georgia at this point (control: the State House anchor returns South Carolina). GEORGIA BECAUSE NO INSTANCE SERVES IT, and on land well clear of the river, whose channel the county fabric could place on either side.
